pride_data.title: Investigation of interaction of p97, p37,  PPI, SDS22 and Inhibitor-3 using cross-linking mass spectrometry (CL-MS)
pride_data.projectDescription: In this project we investigated the complexes PPI/SDS22/Inhibitor-3 and p97/p37/PPI/SDS22/Inhibitor-3 by CL-MS using DSBU as crosslinker.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) was performed as described previously (Pan et al., 2018). Briefly, either 300 µg of p97-SPI complex or 56 µg of SPI complex was dissolved in 200 µL of buffer containing 30 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 300 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP. DSBU (disuccinimidyl dibutyric urea, Alinda Chemical Limited) was added to a final concentration of 3 mM, and the crosslinking reaction was performed at 25 °C for 1 h. The reaction was stopped by adding Tris-HCl pH 8.0 to a final concentration of 100 mM and incubated at 25 °C for 30 min. Crosslinked protein complexes were precipitated by adding 4 volumes of cold acetone and kept at -20°C overnight. Protein pellets were collected by centrifugation, dried at room temperature, and denatured in 8 M urea with 1 mM DTT for 30 min at 25 °C. Cysteine residues were alkylated by adding chloroacetamide to a final concentration of 5.5 mM and incubating at 25 °C for 20 min. Samples were digested by Lys-C (2 µg) at 25 °C for 3 h, followed by trypsin digestion (1 µg) at 25 °C for 16 h. The digestion was stopped by adding trifluoroacetic acid to a final concentration of 0.2%. The resulting peptides were fractionated using a Superdex Peptide 3.2/ 300 column (Cytiva) connected to an ÄKTAmicro FPLC system (GE Healthcare). The SEC runs were performed at a flow rate of 0.1 ml/min with an aqueous eluent containing 30% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid. Fractions containing peptides were collected, dried, and submitted to LC-MS/MS analysis.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS analysis was performed as previously reported (Pan et al., 2018) using a Q-Exactive Plus mass spectrometer (Thermo). Raw data from the Q-Exactive Plus mass spectrometer were converted to Mascot generic files format. Program MeroX version 1.6.6.6 (Gotze et al., 2015) was used for crosslink identification. In the settings of MeroX, the precursor precision and the fragment ion precision were changed to 10.0 and 20.0 ppm, respectively. RISE mode was used, and the maximum missing ion was set to 1. A false discovery rate of 5% was used as the cut-off to exclude the candidates with lower MeroX scores.
